newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds were lower at the close on Wednesday, depressed with most European markets by comments by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing.
"He suggested we are at the bottom of the interest rate cycle in Europe," a dealer in Madrid said.
Issing said there was no reason to expect further reductions in key German interest rates.
On the Spanish market a wait-and-see mood prevails, especially from foreign investors.
"It's been almost a week since we've had any directed movement" one dealer said.
"For tomorrow we don't expect anything except a narrow trading range," a dealer said. After a first support at 107.00 chartists put the next level at around 106.60.
The 10-year spread over German Bunds widened to 183 basis points from 179, while the peseta weakened versus the mark following the other main European crosses.

There was little movement along the yield curve, with the spread of five to 10-year bonds unchanged at around 80 basis points. The three year 7.80 percent bond fell to 102.77 from 102.95 at yesterday's close to yield 6.73 percent.
